_why: Every project on this machine that imports uilab, and how to run its
tests. Consumers install EDITABLE, so they always get the newest code with
no update step -- which means the risk runs the other way: a change here
reaches every consumer instantly, and nothing tells you it broke one until
tools/check_consumers.py reads this file. Adding a project is one entry --
path is relative to THIS repo, so no home directory is published.
Consumers are expected to sit beside it. A missing checkout is SKIPPED,
never failed, so a machine that has not cloned a consumer is not a broken
python is relative to path; verify is argv passed to that interpreter.
Prefer the narrowest suite that would actually catch a uilab regression --
a full suite that takes three minutes gets skipped, and a gate nobody runs
is a gate that does not exist.
